Patient has a history of advanced osteoarthritis, with significant right knee joint degradation. Previous conservative treatments including physical therapy and NSAIDs have been unsuccessful in managing chronic pain and mobility limitations.

- Anesthesia: General + regional nerve block
- Estimated blood loss: 275 mL
- Tourniquet time: 78 minutes
- No immediate complications observed

- Anticoagulation: Enoxaparin 40mg subcutaneous daily
- Early mobilization protocol initiated
- Physical therapy consult for progressive rehabilitation

1. Wound check with orthopedic nursing staff in 10 days
2. Detailed physical therapy assessment in 2 weeks
3. Surgical follow-up with Dr. Chen in 6 weeks

- Oxycodone 5mg, every 4-6 hours PRN pain
- Celecoxib 200mg daily
- Enoxaparin 40mg subcutaneous daily
- Multivitamin supplement

Additional Notes:
Patient educated on home exercise program, wound care, and signs of potential post-surgical complications. Home health nursing services arranged for initial post-discharge support.

On September 15, 2023, Marcus Chen, a 62-year-old patient with advanced Parkinson's disease, was admitted to Stanford Medical Center for a comprehensive deep brain stimulation (DBS) evaluation and potential surgical intervention. Patient contact email: marcus.chen2023@gmail.com, phone: (650) 417-3829.

Dr. Samantha Rodriguez led the comprehensive neurological assessment, focusing on Marcus's progressive motor symptoms and medication management. The patient has been experiencing increasing tremors, rigidity, and reduced mobility over the past 18 months, despite optimal pharmaceutical treatment with carbidopa-levodopa.

Surgical consultation involved detailed imaging studies, including high-resolution MRI and functional neuroimaging to map precise brain targeting. After extensive discussion, the medical team recommended implantation of the Boston Scientific Vercise Gevia™ Deep Brain Stimulation System (Model Number: 4418, Serial Number: BSC-PD-2023-0915).

Preoperative neuropsychological testing revealed mild cognitive impairment, which was carefully considered in the surgical planning. The multidisciplinary team, including neurosurgeons, neurologists, and rehabilitation specialists, developed a comprehensive treatment strategy.

Surgical Procedure Details:
- Bilateral subthalamic nucleus (STN) electrode placement
- Neurostimulator implantation in left chest wall
- Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring
- Total procedure time: 6.5 hours
- Estimated blood loss: 75 mL
- No immediate complications observed

Post-Operative Care Plan:
1. 48-hour intensive neurological monitoring
2. Gradual DBS system programming
3. Medication adjustment
4. Physical and occupational therapy consultation
5. Cognitive rehabilitation support

Discharge Recommendations:
- Strict adherence to rehabilitation protocols
- Scheduled follow-up appointments
- Gradual return to modified daily activities
- Continuous DBS system parameter optimization

The patient and his family were extensively counseled about the potential benefits and risks of the deep brain stimulation intervention, including potential improvements in motor function and quality of life.

Follow-up Schedule:
- Initial device programming: September 22, 2023
- Neurological reassessment: October 15, 2023
- Comprehensive rehabilitation evaluation: November 1, 2023

Additional notes: Patient demonstrated excellent initial recovery with noticeable reduction in tremor amplitude and improved motor control during immediate post-operative assessment.

Preoperative Consultation:
Mr. Chen, a 56-year-old male with a history of renal mass in the left kidney, underwent extensive diagnostic imaging and consultation. Preoperative CT scans revealed a 4.2 cm solid renal tumor in the lower pole of the left kidney, suspicious for clear cell renal carcinoma.

Surgical Procedure:
Dr. Maria Rodriguez performed a da Vinci Xi Surgical System robotic nephrectomy (Serial No: RB-2023-09015). The surgical approach involved:
- Precise robotic-guided tumor resection
- Minimal invasive technique with 4 small incision ports
- Intraoperative frozen section confirmation of tumor margins
- Complete tumor removal with negative surgical margins

Operative Details:
- Anesthesia: General
- Estimated Blood Loss: 125 mL
- Operative Time: 3 hours 15 minutes
- Estimated Tumor Size: 4.2 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm

Postoperative Management:
Patient was monitored in the surgical intensive care unit. Pain management included patient-controlled analgesia with gradual transition to oral medications. Wound healing progressed normally with no signs of infection.

Follow-up Care:
Recommended follow-up and additional resources available at: https://ucsfurology.org/patientresources

Patient Education:
Comprehensive recovery instructions provided, including:
- Wound care protocols
- Activity restrictions
- Medication management
- Scheduled follow-up appointments with oncology and urology

Discharge Plan:
Discharged on September 18, 2023, with instructions for continued recovery and scheduled follow-up imaging in 3 months to monitor for any potential recurrence.
